{
  "dataset_name": "codexglue",
  "model_family": "linear_svm",
  "schema_generator": "claude-sonnet-4.6",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "func_length_normalized",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-normalized length of the function source code string, capturing code size as a smooth continuous feature useful for linear margins",
      "value_range": [0.0, 12.0],
      "feature_family": "code_complexity",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Longer functions tend to have more complex logic and may correlate with vulnerability patterns; log normalization prevents outlier dominance",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(func.str.len())"
    },
    {
      "name": "func_line_count_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-normalized count of newline characters in function code, approximating number of lines",
      "value_range": [0.0, 8.0],
      "feature_family": "code_complexity",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Line count is a proxy for function complexity; log scale smooths distribution for linear SVM",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(func.str.count('\\n'))"
    },
    {
      "name": "pointer_density",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of pointer dereference operators to total function length, measuring pointer usage intensity",
      "value_range": [0.0, 0.05],
      "feature_family": "code_patterns",
      "expected_model_benefit": "High pointer density may indicate memory manipulation code that is more prone to vulnerabilities",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "func.str.count('\\*') / np.maximum(func.str.len(), 1)"
    },
    {
      "name": "conditional_density",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of conditional keywords (if, else, switch) occurrences to line count, measuring branching complexity per line",
      "value_range": [0.0, 2.0],
      "feature_family": "code_complexity",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Dense branching logic increases code paths and may correlate with error-prone code sections",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(func.str.count('\\bif\\b') + func.str.count('\\belse\\b') + func.str.count('\\bswitch\\b')) / np.maximum(func.str.count('\\n'), 1)"
    },
    {
      "name": "memory_op_count_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-normalized count of memory-related function calls (malloc, free, memcpy, memset, realloc, calloc)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 4.0],
      "feature_family": "code_patterns",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Memory management operations are common sources of vulnerabilities; this feature captures their presence",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(func.str.count('malloc|free|memcpy|memset|realloc|calloc'))"
    },
    {
      "name": "error_handling_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of error-handling patterns (return -1, goto fail, NULL checks) to total lines",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "code_patterns",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Functions with more error handling may be more robust; absence of error handling may indicate vulnerability",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(func.str.count('return -1|return NULL|goto fail|goto error|goto out') + func.str.count('== NULL|!= NULL|== 0|< 0')) / np.maximum(func.str.count('\\n'), 1)"
    },
    {
      "name": "project_is_ffmpeg",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Binary indicator for FFmpeg project (1) vs QEMU project (0), encoded as numeric for linear SVM",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "project_metadata",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Different projects may have different vulnerability distributions; this linear projection captures project-level bias",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(project == 'FFmpeg', 1.0, 0.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "commit_frequency_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-normalized frequency of the commit_id in the training set, approximating how many functions share the same commit",
      "value_range": [0.0, 6.0],
      "feature_family": "commit_metadata",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Commits touching many functions may be large refactors or security patches affecting multiple code areas",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": false,
      "formula": "np.log1p(commit_id.map(commit_id.value_counts()))"
    },
    {
      "name": "loop_complexity_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Weighted sum of loop constructs (for, while, do-while) normalized by line count, measuring iteration complexity",
      "value_range": [0.0, 2.0],
      "feature_family": "code_complexity",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Loop-heavy code with complex iteration patterns may have off-by-one errors or buffer overflows",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(func.str.count('\\bfor\\b') + func.str.count('\\bwhile\\b') + func.str.count('\\bdo\\b')) / np.maximum(func.str.count('\\n'), 1)"
    },
    {
      "name": "string_format_risk_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-normalized count of format string and string manipulation functions (sprintf, printf, strcpy, strcat, gets, scanf)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 3.5],
      "feature_family": "code_patterns",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Format string functions and unsafe string operations are classic vulnerability sources",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(func.str.count('sprintf|printf|strcpy|strcat|\\bgets\\b|scanf|strncpy|snprintf'))"
    },
    {
      "name": "vulnerability_keyword_density",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Semantic assessment of how densely the function contains patterns associated with common vulnerability classes: buffer operations, integer arithmetic on sizes, unchecked returns, and unsafe API usage. Score from 0 (no risk patterns) to 1 (high density of risk patterns).",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "semantic_risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures holistic vulnerability signal from code semantics that individual keyword counts may miss; provides smooth continuous score for SVM margin",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "code_structure_complexity_score",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Semantic assessment of structural complexity based on nesting depth indicators, multiple return paths, mixed data types, and function call chains. Score from 0 (simple linear code) to 1 (highly complex nested structure).",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "semantic_risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Complex code structure is harder to reason about and more likely to contain subtle bugs; provides a continuous complexity signal for linear SVM",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
